title: Repeated Register Decrement Run
statement: Let $h$ be a bit string, let $r$ be one of nine registers, let $count$ be a natural number, let $path : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{DropState}$ be a sequence of machine states, and let $v$ assign a natural number to each register. Suppose every register initially holds at most $4|h|+4$, where $|h|$ is the length of $h$, and at each step $i<count$ the instruction in state $path(i)$ decrements register $r$ and moves to $path(i+1)$. Then the machine in mode $mode$, started with state $path(0)$, register values $v$, and no answer, reaches state $path(count)$ with register $r$ decreased by truncated subtraction of $count$, all other registers unchanged, and no answer; throughout the run, every preterminal configuration satisfies the machine's safety condition and every register remains at most $4|h|+4$.
